title: Workplace explainer
when: Benefits, retirement, pay, policy, training, onboarding and client updates at a company or a financial firm: films people are sent, not films they chose
rules: Show each idea as something that changes on its word: coins that stack, a lock that opens, a window on a calendar, a value changed in the app. Start from the workplace sketches (portal, match, vesting, deadline, expire, inspect, choose, split; `find` names the one that fits) and fill their words, moments and numbers.
Keep something on screen across cuts: a cast of the film's own objects (a paycheck, coins, a calendar, a person) that re-forms beat to beat, or one world the camera moves through.
Open on what the viewer could lose or gain in the first five seconds, not on a welcome.

Show the step done in the app (portal) in one sentence, then end on the film's own picture changed (the jar full, the calendar checked, the opening object back), with the deadline in the voice; never on a card that lists it.
Headings only for chapters: the picture and the voice carry each scene.
Figures come from the source document, counted one unit per token or drawn to scale, with the document named in the source line. Plain attribution, no disclaimers.
Warm, plain words. No fear, no jargon without a picture.
